title: Zapoi (Russian)
content: Zapoi (Russian) Two or more days of drunkness usually involving a journey of waking up in an unexpected place.
Uitwaaien (Dutch) The act of going for a walk or to the countryside in order to clear one's mind.
Jayus (Indonesian) A joke so poorly told and so unfunny that one cannot help but laugh.
Tingo (Pascuence) The act of stealing objects one desires from a friend's house by gradually borrowing them.
Litost (Czech) The state of agony and torment created by the sudden sight of one's own misery.
Ikigai (Japanese) One's reason to get up in the morning, one's reason to live.
Dépaysement (French) The feeling, nor good or bad, of being a foreigner; of not being at home, of being in a different place.
Saudade (Portuguese)  A deep emotional state of nostalgic or profound melancholic longing for an absent place, item or person that one cares for and/or loves.
Cafuné (Brazilian Portuguese) The act of running your fingers through someone’s hair in a loving way
Iktsuarpok (Inuktitut) The feeling of anticipation while waiting for someone to arrive, often leading to intermittently going outside to check for them.
Komorebi (Japanese) The sunlight that filters through the leaves of trees.
Goya (Urdu) The transporting suspension of disbelief that happens when fantasy is so realistic that it temporarily becomes reality.
Mångata (Swedish) The road-like reflection of the moon on the water.
Kilig (Tagalog) The sudden thrilling feeling of an inexplicable joy one gets when something romantic  occurs.

Mamihlapinatapei (Yaghan)
The wordless look/exchange shared by two people who both want to initiate something, but are reluctant to do so.
Jijivisha (Hindi) The strong, eternal desire to live and to continue living.
Gluggaveður (Icelandic) The weather that is beautiful to see, but not to be in: windowweather.
Gigil (Tagalog / Filipino) The gritting-of-teeth urge to pinch or squeeze something that is unbearably cute.
Schadenfreude (German) The feeling of pleasure derived from witnessing another's misfortune.
Pochemuchka (Russian) One who asks too many questions.

Avos’
авось (Russian) Blind trust in plain luck.
Chingada (Mexican Spanish) A hellish, imaginary, faraway place where you send all those you annoy you.

Hiraeth (Welsh) Feeling of missing a time, an era, or a person, including homesickness for what may not exist any longer. 


(See 'saudade')
Toska (Russian) A deep melancholy, anxiety or despair without a clear source or cause.
Fernweh (German) Longing for an unseen faraway place.
Torschlusspanik (German) A running-out-of-time stress about the goals one still hasn't accomplished.

Duyên (Vietnamese) 
The tying of fate. The predestined tie that makes people meet each other.
Mokita (New Guinean) The truth everyone knows but nobody says.
Age-otori (Japanese) To look worse after a haircut.
Estrenar (Spanish) To wear or use something for the first time.
Sólarfrí (Icelandic) When employees get an unexpected day or afternoon off to enjoy a particularly sunny and warm day. Sun vacation.
Uitbuiken (Dutch) To take some time to idle after a good meal or between courses. To let your belly out.
Dauwtrappen (Dutch) The feeling of walking barefoot on dew-covered morning grass. Dew-treading.

답정너 – Dab-jeong-neo (Korean)
A situation in which someone asks a question but has already decided the answer they want to hear.
눈치 – Noon-chi (Korean) Being in tune to someone’s feelings and emotions to properly gauge and react to a situation.

썸타다 – Sseom-ta-da (Korean)
An ambiguous stage of dating where you’ve been seeing each other casually but haven’t yet defined the relationship.
Raðljóst (Icelandic) Enough light to find your way by.
Razbliuto (Russian) The feeling a person has for someone they once loved but no longer do.

Desenrascanço (Portuguese from Portugal)
The ability to solve a problem without having the knowledge or the adequate tools to do so, by use of imaginative resources or by applying knowledge to new situations. Also, "MacGyvering."

Waldeinsamkeit (German) 
The feeling of being alone in the woods, solitude, and a connectedness to nature.

Iktsuarpok (Inuit) 
The anticipation and impatient excitement for a visit that makes you look out the window countless times in hope of seeing your guest arrive.

Datsuzoku (Japanese)
To escape from the daily routine, to take a break from the conventions and mundanities of one’s life, to discover more creativity, resourcefulness, and to perceive your surroundings differently.

Verschlimmbessern (German)
Attempting to fix something, but making it worse.

Parea (Greek) 
A stage for the development of friendships and growth of the human spirit.

Abbiocco (Italian, obviously) 
The sleepy, contented feeling that comes after eating a big meal.
Gaupasa (Euskera) To party until the sun rises.
Tripazorri (Euskera) Extreme desire to eat. It literally translates 'lice in your stomach'

Kuchisabishii (Japanese)
When you're not hungry, but you eat because your mouth is lonely.

Mencolek (Indonesia)
Tapping someone on the other side of the shoulder, making them turn into the wrong direction.
Gökotta (Swedish) to rise at dawn in order to go out and listen to the birds sing
Ubuntu (South African) a quality that includes the essential human virtues; compassion and humanity.
Kokoro (Japanese: 心) To use heart, spirit, soul and mind all together, cohesively.

Nankurunaisa (Okinawan - Japanese): Hardship won't come, time will cure it. Everything is gonna be alright. 




(From makuto soke nankurunaisa. makuto soke = If you do the right thing, the true thing” “nankurunaisa = everything is gonna be alright)

Petricor (Spanish, from Greek) The smell of the dry soil after the first 
rain.
Habseligkeiten (German) The paltry belongings of an almost penniless person. What we would pick to take with us if we had to run away without much. "Belongings+soul"
παροινεὶν (Ancient Greek) To say silly things while you're drunk.
Gökotta (Swedish) To wake up early in the morning with the purpose of hearing the first bird sing.

Ukiyo. (Japanese)

living in the moment detached from the bothers of life,  
''the floating world.''

Lagom (Swedish) 
Not too much and not too little, just the right amount.

Ahorita (Spanish)
Now, right now, in a little bit, maybe later, maybe tomorrow, maybe never.

Fremdschämen (German) 
The embarrassment felt when someone else does something awful. 

See Spanish: Pena ajena.

Kalsarikännit (Finnish) 
Getting drunk at home by yourself while only wearing your underwear.

Epibreren (Dutch)
Convincingly acting like you are doing something important when you're actually doing nothing.

Mencomot (Indonesian)
Stealing things of little to no value, just for the fun of it.

Yūgen (Japanese)
A mysterious sense of the beauty of the universe... and the sad beauty of human suffering

Hygge (Danish)
The pleasant and intimate feeling of sitting around a fire with your close friends.

Luftmensh (Yiddish)
An impractical, contemplative, and dreaming person who has no definite business or income.

Fargin (Yiddish) 
To wholeheartedly appreciate the successes of others.

Schapsidee (German)
Ideas so ludicrous that they must have been conceived while drunk.
Frühjahrsmüdigkeit (German) Early year tiredness. The daunting  and dispiriting feeling of the opportunities given by a new beginning —the fear of not being able to do justice to our potential.
U yik’ al jal (Maya) The wind that announces the rain is coming.
Pakiramdam (Tagalog) Listening to your gut, a wholeness of self. A calling that guides us home.
한 / Han (Korean) Beautiful sadness. A feeling of unresolved resentment against injustices suffered, a mixture of sorrow and resentment, but with tinges of hope within the sadness and anger.
恋の予感 / koi no yokan (Japanese) The feeling upon first meeting someone that you will inevitably fall in love with them. *The premonition of love.*
Desbundar (Portuguese) Shedding one's inhibitions in having fun. To renounce a square life and go live as wished.
Kogarashi 木枯らし (Japanese) The cold wind that shakes fall leaves and announces the winter is coming.
Lãng du (Vietnamese) Wandering around with no purpose while feeling sorrow or loneliness.
답답하다 pronounced: dap-dap-ha-da  (Korean) The feeling that there is no good solution to a problem, or that you can’t quite figure out what to do to remedy a situation.

어이없다 pronunced: duh-ee-up-da (Korean) Literally this adjective translates to “without a why.” In practice, it describes a situation that has no reason, or that is so absurd that it leaves you dumbfounded.
Torschlusspanik (German): Last minute panic.
Fremdschämen (German) The feeling of shame on someone else’s behalf.
Schnappsidee (German) An idea you have while drunk that you will probably regret in the morning.
Zweisamkeit (German) The intimacy shared between two people. It indicates a kind of loneliness around a pair who share a special bond. It can be conveyed by the idea of ‘twoness’ or ‘togetherness’.
Stammtisch (German) An informal friendly get-together held regularly, it's also the usually large, often round table around which the group meets. Regular's table.

희망 고문 (Korean) Hope torture, where one is continuously given hope for something that is unlikely to happen, leading to disappointment or despair. It can apply to relationships, the workplace, or everyday issues, where persistent false expectations end up causing more harm than good. 

(huimang gomun)
(積ん読) Tsundoku (Japanese) The habit of letting books pile up unread.
Chutzpah חוצפה(Yiddishh) Audacity mixed with nerve, shameless boldness—often admirable and outrageous at the same time.
Torschlusspanik (German) Literally “gate-closing panic.” That creeping anxiety that time is running out — career, love, youth — the medieval city gates are about to shut.

َشْوَة (nashwa)
(Arabic) A light intoxication, not necessarily from alcohol. Could be joy, power, beauty, or even revenge.

غِبْطَة (ghibṭa)
(Arabic) Envy without malice. Wanting what someone has, but wishing them well.
Tartle (Scots) The panicked hesitation when you have to introduce someone whose name you’ve forgotten.
Backpfeifengesicht  (German) a face begging to be slapped, a very punchable face.
Utepils (Norwegian) the joy of drinking a beer outdoors, especially the first one after a long winter.
